prompt.adult: In the burden against Babylon, the LORD says, “Behold, I will stir up” whom against them?
prompt.child: God warned Babylon that He would send a people against it. Which people did He name?
prompt.teen: Isaiah 13:17: “Behold, I will stir up ___ against them.” Who fills the blank?
prompt.older: According to Isaiah 13:17, which people would the LORD stir up against Babylon?

verses.text: “Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them, Who will not regard silver; And as for gold, they will not delight in it.

explanation.adult: Read the first line of 13:17, after “I will stir up.”
explanation.child: Look at the start of verse 17.
explanation.teen: 13:17 opens with the LORD’s own words. Read the people He names.
explanation.older: It is in the opening line of 13:17.

teaching.extended_explanation: 13:17 adds that this people will not regard silver and will take no delight in gold. 13:19 then turns to Babylon itself, “the glory of kingdoms.”
teaching.takeaway: The LORD would stir up the Medes against Babylon.

review.notes: Fruitful stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _fruitful_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: Isaiah says Babylon, “the glory of kingdoms,” will be like cities God overthrew. Which cities?
prompt.child: God said proud Babylon would be ruined like two cities He had destroyed long before. Which two?
prompt.teen: Isaiah 13:19: Babylon “Will be as when God overthrew” which cities?
prompt.older: According to Isaiah 13:19, Babylon will be as when God overthrew what?

verses.text: And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, The beauty of the Chaldeans’ pride, Will be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.

explanation.adult: Read the last line of 13:19, after “God overthrew.”
explanation.child: Look at the end of verse 19.
explanation.teen: 13:19 closes with a comparison. Read the names in it.

teaching.extended_explanation: 13:19 first calls Babylon “the glory of kingdoms” and “The beauty of the Chaldeans’ pride.” 13:20 adds that it will never be inhabited, and 13:21-22 fill its houses with owls, ostriches, and jackals.
teaching.takeaway: Babylon would be overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah.

prompt.adult: “The earth is violently broken.” In 24:20, the earth shall reel to and fro like what?
prompt.child: Isaiah saw the whole earth shaking back and forth. What did he say it would sway like?
prompt.teen: Isaiah 24:20: “The earth shall reel to and fro like ___.” What fills the blank?
prompt.older: According to Isaiah 24:20, what will the reeling earth be like?

verses.text: The earth is violently broken, The earth is split open, The earth is shaken exceedingly.
The earth shall reel to and fro like a drunkard, And shall totter like a hut; Its transgression shall be heavy upon it, And it will fall, and not rise again.

explanation.adult: Read the first line of 24:20, after “to and fro like.”
explanation.child: Look at the start of verse 20.
explanation.teen: 24:20 opens with one picture and follows with a second. Read the first.
explanation.older: It is near the start of 24:20.

teaching.extended_explanation: 24:19 uses three lines in a row about the earth being broken, split, and shaken. 24:20 then adds a second picture, a tottering hut, and says its transgression is heavy upon it.
teaching.takeaway: The earth shall reel to and fro like a drunkard.

prompt.adult: On “this mountain” the LORD of hosts will make a feast for all people. In 25:6, the first feast is a feast of what?
prompt.child: Isaiah said God will make a great feast for all people on His mountain. What kind of food is named first?
prompt.teen: Isaiah 25:6: “A feast of ___, A feast of wines on the lees.” What fills the blank?
prompt.older: According to Isaiah 25:6, what is the first feast the LORD of hosts will make for all people?

verses.text: And in this mountain The LORD of hosts will make for all people A feast of choice pieces, A feast of wines on the lees, Of fat things full of marrow, Of well-refined wines on the lees.
And He will destroy on this mountain The surface of the covering cast over all people, And the veil that is spread over all nations.

explanation.adult: Read 25:6 after “will make for all people.”
explanation.child: Look at the middle of verse 6, at the first “A feast of.”
explanation.teen: 25:6 names more than one feast. Read the first.
explanation.older: It follows the first “A feast of” in 25:6.

teaching.extended_explanation: 25:6 goes on to wines on the lees and fat things full of marrow. 25:7 adds that on the same mountain the LORD will destroy the covering cast over all people and the veil spread over all nations.
teaching.takeaway: The LORD will make “A feast of choice pieces.”

prompt.adult: In 25:8, what does Isaiah say the LORD will swallow up?
prompt.child: Isaiah said God will swallow something up for good. What will it be?
prompt.teen: Isaiah 25:8: “He will swallow up ___.” What fills the blank?
prompt.older: According to Isaiah 25:8, what will the LORD swallow up?

verses.text: He will swallow up death forever, And the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from all faces; The rebuke of His people He will take away from all the earth; For the LORD has spoken.
And it will be said in that day: “Behold, this is our God; We have waited for Him, and He will save us. This is the LORD; We have waited for Him; We will be glad and rejoice in His salvation.”

explanation.child: Look at the very start of verse 8.
explanation.teen: 25:8 opens with this promise; 25:9 gives the people’s reply. Read the opening line.

teaching.extended_explanation: 25:8 continues with the Lord GOD wiping every face and taking away the rebuke of His people. 25:9 is what they will say in that day: “Behold, this is our God; We have waited for Him, and He will save us.”
teaching.takeaway: He will swallow up death forever.

prompt.adult: In 24:14 they lift up their voice and sing for the majesty of the LORD. In 26:3, how will the LORD keep the one whose mind is stayed on Him?
prompt.child: Isaiah said God will keep a person safe when that person’s mind stays on Him. How will God keep that person?
prompt.teen: Isaiah 26:3: “You will keep him in ___, Whose mind is stayed on You.” What fills the blank?
prompt.older: According to Isaiah 26:3, in what will the LORD keep the one who trusts in Him?

verses.text: They shall lift up their voice, they shall sing; For the majesty of the LORD They shall cry aloud from the sea.
You will keep him in perfect peace, Whose mind is stayed on You, Because he trusts in You.

explanation.adult: Read the first line of 26:3, after “keep him in.”
explanation.child: Look at the start of Isaiah 26:3.
explanation.teen: 24:14 is the setting; 26:3 opens with the promise. Read it.
explanation.older: It is in the opening line of 26:3.

teaching.extended_explanation: 24:14 has voices crying aloud from the sea. 26:3 ends with the reason for the promise: “Because he trusts in You.” 26:4 follows with “Trust in the LORD forever.”
teaching.takeaway: The LORD keeps him “in perfect peace, Whose mind is stayed on You.”

prompt.adult: In 13:10 the sun will be darkened in its going forth. In 24:23 the moon will be disgraced and the sun ashamed, for the LORD of hosts will reign where?
prompt.child: Isaiah said one day the sun and moon would look dim next to God’s glory. Where did he say the LORD would reign as King?
prompt.teen: Isaiah 13:10 darkens the sun. Isaiah 24:23: “For the LORD of hosts will reign On ___ and in Jerusalem.” What fills the blank?
prompt.older: Isaiah 13:10 and 24:23 both speak of the sun. According to 24:23, on what mountain will the LORD of hosts reign?

verses.text: For the stars of heaven and their constellations Will not give their light; The sun will be darkened in its going forth, And the moon will not cause its light to shine.
Then the moon will be disgraced And the sun ashamed; For the LORD of hosts will reign On Mount Zion and in Jerusalem And before His elders, gloriously.

explanation.adult: Read the second half of 24:23, after “will reign On.”
explanation.teen: 13:10 sets the scene; 24:23 names the place. Read the line after “will reign.”
explanation.older: It is in the last lines of 24:23, before “and in Jerusalem.”

teaching.extended_explanation: 13:10 belongs to the burden against Babylon: stars, sun, and moon give no light on the day of the LORD. 24:23 uses the same lights another way. They are put to shame because the LORD of hosts reigns “before His elders, gloriously.”
teaching.takeaway: The LORD of hosts will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem.

prompt.adult: In 25:5 the LORD brings down the song of the terrible ones like heat in the shadow of a cloud. In 26:20 He calls His people into their chambers to hide for a little moment. Until when?
prompt.child: Isaiah said God would tell His people to go inside, shut the doors, and hide for a short time. How long were they to hide?
prompt.teen: Isaiah 26:20: “Hide yourself, as it were, for a little moment, Until ___.” What fills the blank?
prompt.older: Isaiah 25:5 says the LORD will reduce the noise of aliens. According to 26:20, until when should His people hide?

choices.text: the night has turned to day

verses.text: You will reduce the noise of aliens, As heat in a dry place; As heat in the shadow of a cloud, The song of the terrible ones will be diminished.
Come, my people, enter your chambers, And shut your doors behind you; Hide yourself, as it were, for a little moment, Until the indignation is past.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of Isaiah 26:20.
explanation.teen: 25:5 is the setting; 26:20 gives the time. Read its final line.

teaching.extended_explanation: 25:5 pictures the noise of the terrible ones brought low like heat under a cloud. 26:20 opens with “Come, my people, enter your chambers,” and 26:21 says the LORD comes out of His place to punish the inhabitants of the earth.
teaching.takeaway: They hide “Until the indignation is past.”
